2027-01-03.title: First Sunday of Denha (Sunday before Denha)
2027-01-03.readTitle: Readings of the day (First Set; mapped from the official calendar, verify locally)
readings: I have come down to deliver them
Cyrus, the Lord's anointed, called by name
Salvation through faith in Christ Jesus
The Spirit of the Lord is upon me
2027-01-03.alt: The calendar counts this Sunday before the feast as the First Sunday of Denha. 3 January is also the feast of St Kuriakose Elias Chavara (Genesis 12:1–4; Isaiah 44:1–4; 1 Peter 4:12–19; Matthew 5:1–12); where it is kept, follow the local direction. The feast of Denha is on Wednesday 6 January: remind the faithful.
2027-01-03.verse: The Spirit of the Lord is upon me, because he has anointed me to bring good news to the poor.
theo: Three days before the feast of Denha the Church already looks toward the Jordan, where the Spirit will come down upon Jesus. Today's readings speak of God the liberator and of those he sends. At the burning bush God tells Moses: “I have observed the misery of my people who are in Egypt; I have heard their cry on account of their taskmasters. Indeed, I know their sufferings, and I have come down to deliver them.” Then he sends a shepherd who protests, “Who am I that I should go to Pharaoh”, and who receives the only answer that matters: “I will be with you.”

Isaiah goes further. God calls a pagan king, Cyrus of Persia, his anointed, takes him by the right hand and says: “I call you by your name, I surname you, though you do not know me.” If God can use a foreign king to bring his people home from exile, nothing lies outside his reach. Yet Moses and Cyrus are only signs. In the synagogue of Nazareth Jesus unrolls the scroll of Isaiah and reads: “The Spirit of the Lord is upon me, because he has anointed me to bring good news to the poor.” Then he sits down and, with every eye fixed on him, says: “Today this scripture has been fulfilled in your hearing.” The true Anointed, the Mshiha, has come. The freedom he brings is freedom from sin and death, and it begins with the poor.

St Paul shows how this freedom reaches every generation. He reminds Timothy of the faith he received at home: “from childhood you have known the sacred writings that are able to instruct you for salvation through faith in Christ Jesus.” Faith passes from parent to child and from teacher to pupil, and it holds firm through persecution. St Kuriakose Elias Chavara, whose feast falls today, lived this: a son of Kainakary who, like Moses, heard the cry of his people, and who asked that a school stand beside every church, so that every child might come to know the Scriptures and the way of salvation.
conn: This year the calendar counts the Sunday that falls before the feast of 6 January as the First Sunday of Denha. Its readings already sound the theme of the season: God revealing the one he has anointed and sent.

The bush burned but was not consumed (Exodus 3:2). Eastern Fathers, among them St Gregory of Nyssa, saw in it an image of the Virgin Mary, who carried the divine fire in her womb and was not consumed.
Cyrus II of Persia took Babylon in 539 BC and allowed the exiles to return and rebuild the Temple (Ezra 1:1–4). He is the only non-Israelite in the Old Testament called the Lord's anointed.
Jesus reads Isaiah 61:1–2, with a phrase from Isaiah 58:6. He stops before the words about the day of vengeance: he comes first to proclaim the year of the Lord's favour.
St Paul praises the sincere faith that lived first in Timothy's grandmother Lois and his mother Eunice (2 Timothy 1:5). The Scriptures he knew from childhood were learned at home.
St Kuriakose Elias Chavara (1805–1871), co-founder of the CMI and founder of the CMC congregations, pioneered schools beside churches and printed Malayalam books at Mannanam. Canonised in 2014.
altar: The Holy Qurbana is our synagogue of Nazareth: the Word is proclaimed, and the Church believes that in Christ it is fulfilled today. What is proclaimed from the bema is given at the altar.
At the altar the Anointed One, on whom the Spirit rests, comes down to his people as God came down at the burning bush: not to consume us but to set us free.

live: Find out one real need in your parish or neighbourhood this week and do something about it.
When you feel unworthy of a task God gives you, pray: Lord, you will be with me.
Read a Gospel passage aloud with your children or grandchildren before Denha.
Support a poor child's education this year.
fathers: Blessed was that synagogue in which the eyes of all were fixed on Jesus. May our assemblies also look on him; when the eyes of the heart are fixed on the Word, his light shines on our faces.
The light that shone from a thorn bush without burning it shows the mystery of the Virgin: from her the divine light shone into our life, and her virginity was not consumed.
magis: God reveals his name at the burning bush.
Jesus, the Christ, the Anointed One.
The Spirit of the Lord upon the Messiah (Luke 4:18).
Parents, the first educators in the faith.
saints: 3 Jan: St Kuriakose Elias Chavara. 6 Jan: Denha (Baptism of the Lord). 8 Jan: St John the Baptist (First Friday of Denha).
2027-01-03.prayer: Lord Jesus, Anointed of the Father, the Spirit of the Lord is upon you, and you came to bring good news to the poor and release to the captives. You hear our cry as God heard Israel at the burning bush. Send us, as you sent Moses, with the promise that you will be with us; keep us in the faith we learned from childhood; and through the prayers of St Kuriakose Elias Chavara make our homes and schools places where your word is loved. Glory to you with the Father and the Holy Spirit, for ever. Amen.

quick: God hears the cry of his people and comes down to set them free.

Faith learned from childhood leads to salvation.

2027-01-03.special: First Sunday of Denha (Sunday before Denha). St Kuriakose Elias Chavara. Denha on Wednesday.
term: Syriac for the Anointed One, in Greek Christos. Isaiah gives the title even to Cyrus; Jesus is the Anointed in the full sense, anointed with the Holy Spirit (Luke 4:18; Acts 10:38).

family.explain: Jesus went to the synagogue in Nazareth, the town where he grew up. He read from the book of Isaiah: the Spirit of the Lord is upon me, to bring good news to the poor. Then he said: today this has come true!
family.intention: We pray for the poor, the sick and all who need to be set free.
family.ask: Ask: “What good news can our family bring to someone this week?”

illus: As Vicar General, St Chavara issued a circular in 1864 asking that every parish church have a school beside it, a 'pallikkoodam'. Many of the first pupils were poor children who had never held a book. Generations later, Kerala's literacy owes much to that simple rule: the Father's house and the school side by side.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you read the Scriptures in Nazareth and said: today they are fulfilled. Fulfil your word in us as we gather in your name. Amen.
share: I have heard their cry (Exodus 3:7). Whose cry do I hear around me?
Who am I that I should go? I will be with you (Exodus 3:11–12). Where do I feel unworthy, and how does God's promise help me?
Today this scripture has been fulfilled in your hearing (Luke 4:21). Which word of God does Jesus want to fulfil in me today?
pm.resp: Lord, send us with your Spirit.
interc: For the Church, that she may bring good news to the poor.
For those who are captive, oppressed or forgotten.
For rulers and leaders, that God may use them, as he used Cyrus, for the good of his people.
For parents, grandparents and teachers who hand on the faith, through the prayers of St Chavara.
For our group, that we may hear the cry of those around us.
pm.close: Father, you anointed your Son with the Holy Spirit to set your people free. Hear the cry of all who suffer, and make us faithful messengers of your good news. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, in three days we will celebrate Denha, when the Spirit came down upon Jesus at the Jordan. Today's readings prepare us by showing God as the one who hears, comes down and sets free.

Moses is keeping sheep in the wilderness when he sees a bush that burns without being consumed. From the fire God calls him by name and says: I have observed the misery of my people; I have heard their cry; I know their sufferings, and I have come down to deliver them (Exodus 3:7–8). Our God is not deaf to the cries of his people.

Moses protests: who am I that I should go to Pharaoh? God does not tell him how gifted he is. He says only: I will be with you (Exodus 3:11–12). That promise is enough for every mission, every vocation, every difficult task.

In Isaiah God does something more surprising still. He calls Cyrus, a foreign king, his anointed, and says: I call you by your name, though you do not know me (Isaiah 45:4). God can use anyone to save his people. But Cyrus is only a shadow. In Nazareth Jesus stands up in the synagogue and reads: the Spirit of the Lord is upon me, because he has anointed me to bring good news to the poor. Then he says: today this scripture has been fulfilled in your hearing (Luke 4:18, 21). The true Anointed, the Mshiha, is here.

How does this good news reach us? St Paul reminds Timothy that from childhood he has known the sacred writings that instruct him for salvation through faith in Christ Jesus (2 Timothy 3:15). Faith comes to us through families, catechism teachers and parishes, from one generation to the next.

Today we also celebrate St Kuriakose Elias Chavara. Like Moses, he heard the cry of his people, the poor and the unlettered, and he answered by asking that a school stand beside every church. Let us ask for his spirit: to hear the cry of the poor, to trust the promise I will be with you, and to hand on the word of God to our children. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus went to the synagogue in his home town and read from the Bible: God has sent me to bring good news to the poor! Then he said: today it has come true.
St Chavara wanted every child to learn to read, so that they could know God's word. Let us read a little of the Bible with our family this week.

intro: Theme: “Today this scripture has been fulfilled in your hearing.”
God hears, sends and anoints: from the burning bush to Nazareth.

sub: The bush burns but is not consumed.
God sees the misery of his people.
q: Then the LORD said, “I have observed the misery of my people who are in Egypt; I have heard their cry on account of their taskmasters. Indeed, I know their sufferings,

The Spirit of the Lord is upon me, because he has anointed me to bring good news to the poor. He has sent me to proclaim release to the captives and recovery of sight to the blind, to let the oppressed go free,
points.apply: Find one person in need this week and help them.

points.h: Who am I? I will be with you
sub: God offers no flattery, only his presence.
Every mission rests on this promise.
q: He said, “I will be with you; and this shall be the sign for you that it is I who sent you: when you have brought the people out of Egypt, you shall worship God on this mountain.”
And remember, I am with you always, to the end of the age.
points.apply: Take up one task you have been avoiding, trusting God's presence.

q: I will give you the treasures of darkness and riches hidden in secret places, so that you may know that it is I, the LORD, the God of Israel, who call you by your name.
Then he began to say to them, “Today this scripture has been fulfilled in your hearing.”
Keep these words that I am commanding you today in your heart. Recite them to your children and talk about them when you are at home and when you are away, when you lie down and when you rise.

But as for you, continue in what you have learned and firmly believed, knowing from whom you learned it, and how from childhood you have known the sacred writings that are able to instruct you for salvation through faith in Christ Jesus.
points.apply: Pray and read Scripture with your children this week.

concl: The God of the burning bush has come down in Jesus, the Anointed.
St Chavara shows the fruit: faith handed on, the poor raised up.
2027-01-03.resolve: Prepare for Denha on Wednesday with a family reading of the Gospel and a good confession.
